meta.auditType: External audit (no Search Console or analytics access)

client.name: Example Villas
client.subject: A pool villa developer's site in a fictional resort market: technical SEO, content, answer-engine readiness and a 90 day plan.

scoreNotes.SEO, technical: Broken sitemap, slow first byte, template leftovers
scoreNotes.SEO, content and structure: A blog exists; the homepage sells three things at once
scoreNotes.GEO, visibility in AI systems: llms.txt points at a demo domain
scoreNotes.Off-page and trust: Portal listings exist, brand name collides
scoreNotes.Conversion and UX: Form works, price is a placeholder

summary.lead: The site is a working marketing page for a villa developer. Search engines index about 18 pages, an eight-article blog is live and FAQ markup is in place. It does not work as a search engine asset yet: the sitemap answers 404, the homepage description carries a form shortcode, and the AI index describes another business.
summary.verdict: The site is not invisible, it is misread. Three technical defects and a homepage that sells three products at once cost it most of its organic potential. Every critical item can be fixed inside two weeks.
priorities: Technical foundation: sitemap, meta description, llms.txt, utility pages out of the index.
Demand-led structure: one page per project, one per location, one buyer guide.
Trust content: sourced ownership answers, comparison tables and a FAQ that answer engines can quote.

rows: WordPress, page builder, commerce plugin, forms plugin
Two villa projects presented on one homepage
overview.note: Three offers share the homepage: a price headline with a placeholder, a block about a seven-villa project and a block about a second phase with overlapping copy. A visitor and a crawler both leave unsure which product the site sells.

critical.title: XML sitemap answers 404
critical.text: robots.txt points at sitemap_index.xml and the server returns 404. Search engines crawl without a map: slower and less complete.

critical.title: Homepage meta description contains a form shortcode
critical.text: The description field holds an encoded form tag. In results it renders as technical garbage instead of a sales sentence.

critical.title: llms.txt describes a demo site
critical.text: The file exists, which is a positive signal, but its links go to a template demo domain with unrelated products. An AI system reading it may misidentify the business.

critical.title: Commerce utility pages are indexable
critical.text: Shop, compare and wishlist pages carry index directives and demo products. They add noise to a 21 page index.

checks.comment: single request from the auditor, not a lab test

checks.comment: blocks zoom: bad for accessibility and mobile SEO

strengths: FAQ block on the homepage, a base for answer engines
Enquiry form with a budget field
Key features with figures: 7 villas, 240 sqm plots
weaknesses: Title and description do not name the product or the place
No single H1 with the project name and a real price
The ownership FAQ is one sentence where buyers need a table
Two different office addresses in the footer

works: Question and answer format in the FAQ block
blocks: Ownership answers too short: no lease route, no risks
No comparison tables for ownership options
No sourced yield or price figures
aeo.recommendation: Publish one buyer guide with tables on ownership routes, fees and timeline, written so that a single paragraph can be quoted as the answer.

rows: Schema present, but content confuses two project names
The brand name matches a residential district in another country
geo.callout: Brand collision: for the bare brand name, search engines show a district elsewhere rather than the developer. Use the brand together with the place in titles, schema and external profiles.

listed: Two property portals carry the project with prices
One aggregator carries a developer profile
One agency page carries villa specifications
offpage.note: Portal listings drive discovery, but the authority accrues to the portals. The owned site's job is to become the primary source the portals link to.

limitations: Google Search Console: no impressions, clicks or query data
Analytics: no traffic or behaviour data
Keyword and backlink tools: not used in the external tier
Lab performance report: not run; the first-byte figure is a single request

roadmap.title: Critical, quick wins
items: Fix the XML sitemap and confirm the URL in robots.txt answers 200
Rewrite the homepage title and description; remove the shortcode
Rewrite llms.txt for the actual business; remove demo links
Set noindex on shop, compare and wishlist
One H1 on the homepage with the project name and a real starting price

roadmap.title: Foundation
items: Project page with prices, plans and FAQ
Buyer guide with ownership routes and fees
Location page with map and distances
Search Console and Bing Webmaster connected
One product line on the homepage, or two clearly separated

roadmap.title: Organic growth, AEO and GEO
items: Product and place schema on villa pages
PR and mentions in local property media
Business profile for the office and the project location
FAQ expanded to 15 to 20 sourced answers
Comparison tables for ownership, fees and timeline

closing: A beautiful site and a search asset are not the same thing. This one is pointed the right way, with a blog, a FAQ and schema, but was never cleaned up after launching on a template. The critical items take two weeks and show in Search Console within 30 to 60 days.
